missing_units.reason: No unit owns how the reindex embed step recovers from a failure. The wildcard unit touched embed.py and said 'Peer units own resource exhaustion, so no further checks here.' The glean-query unit covers only the query side. Source facts: every reindex starts the embed loop at last=0 (backend.py:1441). It selects embedding IS NULL rows by ascending chunk id (embed.py:172-182). It stops the whole step at the first page that has a provider failure (backend.py:1466-1468: stopped_by, then break). A failed batch is never split, skipped or marked. So a batch the provider refuses every time is retried at the head of every run, and the chunks after it are never embedded. That includes chunks other principals write later, because new chunks get higher ids. Batches are sized by estimate_tokens = ceil(len/4) with 5/6 headroom (embed.py:60,108-129), but the shipped OpenAI provider declares hard caps of 300,000 tokens per request and 8,192 per input. Text at about 1 to 4 tokens per character (CJK, rare scripts, emoji) fills a batch planned at about 250k estimated tokens, which is about 1M characters, with far more real tokens than the cap. truncated_for (embed.py:136-143) uses the same estimate, so it does not catch per-input overflow either. Hypothesis for the hunter: any principal that can write ordinary text can stop vector-index freshness for every principal on the store. Glean's vector leg then goes stale, and reindex reports warnings forever. This is the catalogue's poison-record and head-of-line class. Settle it offline with a fake provider that enforces the declared caps by byte or character count: check whether the loop wedges, whether later principals' chunks stay unembedded, and whether any per-row quarantine exists, like the render pass's quarantined path (backend.py:1317).
